sentences.zh: 法国在1870-71年的普法战争中战败。

sentences.en: And Germany has been created off the back of that.
sentences.zh: 德国就是在那个背景下建立起来的。

sentences.en: And the French feel terribly humiliated because they've also lost Alsace-Lorraine to the Germans.
sentences.zh: 法国人感到极其羞辱，因为他们还失去了阿尔萨斯-洛林给德国人。

sentences.en: And a lot of people from Alsace play a part in the Dreyfus case story.
sentences.zh: 而且很多来自阿尔萨斯的人在德雷福斯案的故事中扮演了角色。

sentences.en: There's lots of people in the army from Alsace.
sentences.zh: 军队里有很多来自阿尔萨斯的人。

sentences.en: And there's this burning sense of kind of mutilation and humiliation that they want these territories back.
sentences.zh: 有一种强烈的被肢解和羞辱的感觉，他们想要回这些领土。

sentences.en: But Germany is the powerhouse of Europe.
sentences.zh: 但德国是欧洲的强国。

sentences.en: So the chances of them getting them back are slim.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拿回领土的机会很渺茫。

sentences.en: And the French, there's a sort of sense in France in the 1890s and so on that there's a kind of a toxicity to politics.
sentences.zh: 法国人，在19世纪90年代的法国有一种感觉，政治有一种毒性。

sentences.en: The political life is poisoned, really, by the humiliations of the century.
sentences.zh: 政治生活确实被那个世纪的羞辱所毒害了。

sentences.en: And the French are very anxious that the Germans have overtaken them technologically and that they're spying on them and stealing all their secrets.
sentences.zh: 法国人非常担心德国人在技术上已经超越了他们，并且在监视他们，窃取他们所有的秘密。

sentences.en: And French military intelligence basically starts spying on the German embassy in Paris.
sentences.zh: 法国军事情报局基本上开始监视德国驻巴黎大使馆。

sentences.en: And they have a housekeeper called Madame Bastion, who is a – she's working for the French secret service.
sentences.zh: 他们有一位管家叫巴斯蒂安夫人，她是——她为法国特勤局工作。

sentences.en: And she's basically spying on the Germans and she finds a torn-up note in a waste paper basket, which becomes known as the bordereau, which means – I don't know what that means.
sentences.zh: 她基本上在监视德国人，她在废纸篓里发现了一张撕碎的纸条，后来被称为“bordereau”，意思是——我不知道那是什么意思。

sentences.en: Let's say a torn-up note.
sentences.zh: 我们就说是张撕碎的纸条吧。

sentences.en: Anyway, she finds this bordereau and she – and it's – they stitch it back together.
sentences.zh: 总之，她发现了这张纸条，然后他们把它拼凑起来。

sentences.en: And they find that it's basically a – the details of a gun, of a new sort of hydraulic-powered gun that the French have developed.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这基本上是——一种枪支的细节，一种法国人开发的液压动力新式枪支。

sentences.en: And somebody has given this to the German military attaché, who's a man called Max von Schwarzkoppen.
sentences.zh: 有人把它给了德国军事专员，一个叫马克斯·冯·施瓦茨科彭的人。

sentences.en: Basically, the sort of casting agency has supplied German officers now.
sentences.zh: 基本上，选角机构现在提供了德国军官。

sentences.en: And they look around to find out who it is.
sentences.zh: 他们四处寻找，想查出是谁干的。

sentences.en: It must be somebody in artillery, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 一定是炮兵里的某个人，等等等等。

sentences.en: And basically, suspicion falls on Dreyfus for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 基本上，怀疑落在了德雷福斯身上，原因有两个。

sentences.en: Reason – well, three reasons, actually.
sentences.zh: 原因——嗯，其实是三个原因。

sentences.en: Reason number one is that he's from Alsace.
sentences.zh: 第一个原因是他是阿尔萨斯人。

sentences.en: So there's this sort of – Alsace has this strange place in the French psyche at this point because, obviously, it's the territory they want to recapture.
sentences.zh: 所以有这种——阿尔萨斯在当时的法国人心理中有着奇怪的地位，因为显然，那是他们想要夺回的领土。

sentences.en: But also, people from Alsace, some of them do feel German rather than French.
sentences.zh: 但也因为，有些阿尔萨斯人确实觉得他们是德国人而不是法国人。

sentences.en: So there is this sort of dubiousness about Dreyfus.
sentences.zh: 所以对德雷福斯有这种怀疑。

sentences.en: Next, Dreyfus is a very chilly character.
sentences.zh: 其次，德雷福斯是一个非常冷漠的人。

sentences.en: He doesn't have lots of friends.
sentences.zh: 他没有很多朋友。

sentences.en: He's not a man to go to the pub with.
sentences.zh: 他不是那种会去酒吧的人。

sentences.en: He's –
sentences.zh: 他是——

sentences.en: Well, he's like the stereotype of a British officer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他就像英国军官的刻板印象。

sentences.en: A little bit, yeah.
sentences.zh: 有点像，是的。

sentences.en: A chilly, stiff upper lip.
sentences.zh: 冷漠，不动声色。

sentences.en: Is he sort of Douglas Jardine to use a cricket scene?
sentences.zh: 用板球场景来说，他算是道格拉斯·贾丁吗？

sentences.en: He's Douglas Jardine, yes.
sentences.zh: 他就是道格拉斯·贾丁，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so all that thing you were describing about his refusal to show any emotion, when this unspeakable humiliation, public humiliation, is being visited by him.
sentences.zh: 所以你描述的关于他拒绝表现出任何情绪的事情，当这种无法言喻的羞辱，公开的羞辱，降临到他身上时。

sentences.en: Oh, a public humiliation, which is literally called a degradation.
sentences.zh: 哦，一种公开的羞辱，字面上被称为“降级”。

sentences.en: A degradation.
sentences.zh: 降级。

sentences.en: I mean, that's its official title.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是它的正式名称。

sentences.en: And he – you know, he –
sentences.zh: 而他——你知道，他——

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He draws on the inner ice.
sentences.zh: 他内心冰冷。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实如此。

sentences.en: And then Robert Harris has an absolutely wonderful novel about the Dreyfus affair.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·哈里斯有一部关于德雷福斯事件的非常精彩的小说。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's great.
sentences.zh: 是的，那部很棒。

sentences.en: What's it called?
sentences.zh: 叫什么名字？

sentences.en: An Officer and a Spy, is it?
sentences.zh: 是《军官与间谍》吗？

sentences.en: I think something like that.
sentences.zh: 我想是类似的名字。

sentences.en: And it's amazing because you know exactly what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 而且它很神奇，因为你知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: And you keep turning pages to find out what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 但你还是会不停地翻页，想知道到底会发生什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, agreed.
sentences.zh: 没错，同意。

sentences.en: I think it's – for me, it's actually his best novel.
sentences.zh: 我认为——对我来说，这其实是他最好的小说。

sentences.en: And in that, one of the really interesting things in that is it would be a much more Hollywood story if Dreyfus was kind of terribly sentimental.
sentences.zh: 在书中，一个非常有趣的点是，如果德雷福斯非常多愁善感，那会是一个更像好莱坞的故事。

sentences.en: Tom Hanks.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·汉克斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, if he was Tom Hanks.
sentences.zh: 没错，如果他是汤姆·汉克斯的话。

sentences.en: But he's absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 但他绝对不是。

sentences.en: He's played by a sort of – he'd be played by some sort of, you know, British character actor who might otherwise be playing Neville Chamberlain or something.
sentences.zh: 他会被某种——他会被某种，你知道，英国性格演员扮演，那种平时可能扮演内维尔·张伯伦之类角色的演员。

sentences.en: That's interesting, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 那很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Jeremy Irons.
sentences.zh: 杰瑞米·艾恩斯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And because he's so unlovable, that kind of gives an extra layer of irony, I suppose, to the story.
sentences.zh: 因为他太不可爱了，我想这给故事增加了一层额外的讽刺意味。

sentences.en: But of course, the big thing about Dreyfus is that he's Jewish.
sentences.zh: 但当然，关于德雷福斯最重要的一点是他是个犹太人。

sentences.en: And anti-Semitism is really, really rampant in France in the 1890s and 1900s.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪90年代和20世纪初的法国，反犹太主义非常非常猖獗。

sentences.en: It's a sort of, I don't know, it's a reaction against modernity.
sentences.zh: 这是一种，我不知道，这是对现代性的一种反动。

sentences.en: It's a search for scapegoats after defeat in war.
sentences.zh: 这是战争失败后寻找替罪羊的行为。

sentences.en: And there's this all this sort of – there's this kind of Catholic conservative politics kind of bubbling away.
sentences.zh: 而且有所有这些——有一种天主教保守派政治在酝酿。

sentences.en: And Dreyfus makes the perfect person.
sentences.zh: 而德雷福斯成了完美的人选。

sentences.en: And once the military have seized on Dreyfus and they've said it's him,
sentences.zh: 一旦军方抓住了德雷福斯，他们说就是他，

sentences.en: they refuse to accept – a lot of the officers refuse to accept any questioning or to entertain any doubts at all.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝接受——很多军官拒绝接受任何质疑，或者根本不愿考虑任何怀疑。

sentences.en: Well, isn't it worse than that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，难道不是更糟吗？

sentences.en: I mean, they frame them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们陷害他。

sentences.en: They start forging.
sentences.zh: 他们开始伪造。

sentences.en: Yeah, they start forging evidence.
sentences.zh: 没错，他们开始伪造证据。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And that's what makes it so toxic, is that actually it kind of ends up where people have to decide either Dreyfus is guilty or the army.
sentences.zh: 这就是让它如此有毒的原因，实际上它最终导致人们必须决定，要么德雷福斯有罪，要么军队有罪。

sentences.en: Yeah, or the army have been lying to you.
sentences.zh: 没错，或者军队一直在对你撒谎。

sentences.en: Because once the army start forging evidence – and I think they do it at first, the honour of the army is at stake.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦军队开始伪造证据——我想他们起初这样做是因为军队的荣誉岌岌可危。

sentences.en: Dreyfus must be proved to be guilty.
sentences.zh: 德雷福斯必须被证明是有罪的。

sentences.en: And once they've started doing that – because quite quickly, within a few years, suspicion falls on another man called Esterhazy, who is, in fact, the guilty party.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们开始这样做——因为很快，几年之内，怀疑就落在了另一个人身上，叫埃斯特哈齐，他实际上才是真正的罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: And then it starts to get taken up by kind of liberal or left-wing rights.
sentences.zh: 然后它开始被自由派或左翼权利所关注。

sentences.en: Emil Zola.
sentences.zh: 埃米尔·左拉。

sentences.en: Most famously, Emil Zola, who writes the front-page story Jacuzze, in which he basically says the entire French establishment – Which he writes when he's in exile, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 最著名的是埃米尔·左拉，他写了头版文章《我控诉》，在文中他基本上说整个法国体制——这是他在流亡时写的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, he has to go into exile, because you see the Dreyfus case become so incendiary that to take a side on it means – I mean,
sentences.zh: 是的，他不得不流亡，因为你看到德雷福斯案件变得如此具有煽动性，以至于站在哪一边都意味着——我是说，

sentences.en: it's far greater than – far more incendiary than Brexit.
sentences.zh: 它远比——远比英国脱欧更具煽动性。

sentences.en: It means you absolutely identify yourself politically in the eyes of your contemporaries, and it means that half the country will hate you,
sentences.zh: 这意味着你在同时代人眼中绝对确定了自己的政治立场，这意味着半个国家会恨你，

sentences.en: because either you are on the side of Dreyfus and of sort of justice, or you're on the side of the army and the honour of France and the nation and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为你要么站在德雷福斯和正义这一边，要么站在军队和法国荣誉、国家以及所有这些东西这一边。

sentences.en: It's very good in ProuSt.
sentences.zh: 在普鲁斯特的作品里写得很好。

sentences.en: I've never read ProuSt.
sentences.zh: 我从没读过普鲁斯特。

sentences.en: Oh, it's so good.
sentences.zh: 哦，它太棒了。

sentences.en: It's really brilliant.
sentences.zh: 真的很精彩。

sentences.en: It looks terribly long.
sentences.zh: 它看起来太长了。

sentences.en: I mean, it is very long.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它确实很长。

sentences.en: I mean, it's indisputably very long, but as a portrait of French society in this period, it's kind of incomparable.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它无可争议地非常长，但作为那个时期法国社会的写照，它是无可比拟的。

sentences.en: And a Proust, obviously, would be a Dreyfus partisan, wouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 而普鲁斯特显然会是德雷福斯的支持者，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, because he's Jewish, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为他是犹太人，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But people's attitudes to Dreyfus is kind of very useful signifier as to where they stand on a whole host of other issues.
sentences.zh: 但人们对德雷福斯的态度是一个非常有用的标志，表明他们在其他一系列问题上的立场。

sentences.en: So to cut a long story short, I think we should definitely do a whole podcast on the Dreyfus case, because it's such a fascinating story.
sentences.zh: 所以长话短说，我认为我们绝对应该专门做一期关于德雷福斯案件的播客，因为它是一个如此引人入胜的故事。

sentences.en: But those of you who don't know how it ends probably do want to know how it ends.
sentences.zh: 但你们中那些不知道结局的人可能确实想知道结局。

sentences.en: So Dreyfus is eventually pardoned.
sentences.zh: 所以德雷福斯最终被赦免了。

sentences.en: He's not exonerated at firSt.
sentences.zh: 他起初并没有被平反。

sentences.en: He's basically found guilty again, completely unfairly, but the French president gives him a pardon, which Dreyfus accepts very reluctantly, because, of course,
sentences.zh: 他基本上再次被判有罪，完全是不公正的，但法国总统给了他特赦，德雷福斯非常不情愿地接受了，因为当然，

sentences.en: accepting a pardon carries the imputation of guilt, and he knows he wasn't guilty.
sentences.zh: 接受特赦带有有罪的暗示，而他知道他没有罪。

sentences.en: But he accepts it.
sentences.zh: 但他接受了。

sentences.en: He's persuaded to accept it.
sentences.zh: 他被说服接受了。

sentences.en: He's not exonerated until 1906.
sentences.zh: 直到1906年他才被平反。

sentences.en: And then he actually serves in the French army in World War I.
sentences.zh: 然后他实际上在第一次世界大战中在法国军队服役。

sentences.en: And even then, you know, nobody really likes him.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，你知道，也没人真正喜欢他。

sentences.en: Even the people who've supported him say, God, he's such a chilly kind of unlovable character, but to who has become this great martyr.
sentences.zh: 即便是那些支持他的人也说，天哪，他真是个冷漠又不可爱的人，但他却成了这样一位伟大的殉道者。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing now is that the French kind of ultra right-wing polemicist, demagogue, and kind of presidential, Eric Zemmour, who is himself Jewish,
sentences.zh: 但现在有趣的是，法国那位极右翼论战者、煽动家，同时也是总统候选人的埃里克·泽穆尔，他本人也是犹太人，

sentences.en: has brought the Dreyfus case back up again and says he thinks Dreyfus was possibly guilty.
sentences.zh: 又把德雷福斯案件翻了出来，并声称他认为德雷福斯可能是有罪的。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly what France needs at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我想这正是法国目前所需要的。

sentences.en: To reopen the Dreyfus case.
sentences.zh: 重审德雷福斯案。

sentences.en: Well, it would make Britain's arguments about Brexit look, you know, restrained and dignified by comparison, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，相比之下，这会让英国关于脱欧的争论看起来既克制又体面，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, Eric Zemmour, I mean, he has – so he also thinks that Marshall Petter was unfairly treated, and he thinks that Dreyfus was guilty.
sentences.zh: 是的，埃里克·泽穆尔，我的意思是，他——他也认为贝当元帅受到了不公正的对待，而且他认为德雷福斯是有罪的。

sentences.en: Shocking.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊。

sentences.en: I mean, these seem unnecessary places to be ripping off at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些似乎是目前没必要去撕开的伤口。

sentences.en: This is not where – if you're just a controversialist, this is just where you end up being led.
sentences.zh: 这不是——如果你只是个好争论的人，这只会是你最终被引向的地方。

sentences.en: You just end up – we must not do that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你最终会——我们绝不能那样做，汤姆。

sentences.en: No, we mustn't.
sentences.zh: 不，我们绝不能。

sentences.en: We must stay on the straight and narrow and avoid taking ludicrous positions.
sentences.zh: 我们必须走正道，避免采取荒谬的立场。

sentences.en: Unnecessary, polemical positions.
sentences.zh: 那些不必要的、好辩的立场。

sentences.en: Yeah, we would never do that, would we?
sentences.zh: 是啊，我们永远不会那样做，对吧？

sentences.en: We'd never, ever do that.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会那样做。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不会。

sentences.en: Anyway, Dreyfus was clearly – he was clearly innocent, so we're not going to do it on the Dreyfus case.
sentences.zh: 总之，德雷福斯显然——他显然是无辜的，所以我们不会在德雷福斯案上那样做。

sentences.en: So that's the Dreyfus affair.
sentences.zh: 这就是德雷福斯事件。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a sad story, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为那是一个悲伤的故事。

sentences.en: Poor Dreyfus.
sentences.zh: 可怜的德雷福斯。

sentences.en: That's an incredibly sad story.
sentences.zh: 那是一个极其悲伤的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, well, it's actually – it's kind of a slight echo of Torvi as a slave, of kind of dynamics of race leading to, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，好吧，实际上——这有点像托尔维作为奴隶的经历，那种种族动态导致了，你知道的，

sentences.en: someone being uprooted from the society in which they belong and sent away to suffer appallingly away from their family and everybody.
sentences.zh: 一个人被从他们所属的社会中连根拔起，被送走去遭受可怕的折磨，远离他们的家人和所有人。

sentences.en: Cosmic injustice.
sentences.zh: 宇宙级的不公。

sentences.en: Cosmic injustice.
sentences.zh: 宇宙级的不公。

sentences.en: Yeah, cosmic injustice, which I guess is why it still has the kind of resonance that it does today.
sentences.zh: 是的，宇宙级的不公，我想这就是为什么它在今天仍然能引起共鸣的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Golly, this series is getting very depressing.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这个系列节目变得非常压抑。

sentences.en: I think we've got one more day, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 我想我们还有最后一天，对吧？

sentences.en: We've got a great one tomorrow, a really cheering one.
sentences.zh: 我们明天有一个很棒的节目，一个真正令人振奋的节目。

sentences.en: We've got one, and we've got the appearance of Samuel Pepys at laSt.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个，而且我们终于要迎来塞缪尔·佩皮斯的登场了。

sentences.en: I don't think we've had enough peeps in these 12 days.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在这12天里，我们对佩皮斯的了解还不够多。
